title: GBRG Supply-Chain Risk <-> BIAN / FICO Crosswalk (governed)
description: Binds the software supply-chain operational-risk control taxonomy to the estate's GOVERNED ontology and, through it, to recognized banking architecture (BIAN service domains) and decisioning (FICO capabilities). Consumed (not forked) from software_supply_chain_operational_risk_framework_v0_2_bian_fico.xlsx (sheets: Ontology, Controls_Evidence, BIAN_Crosswalk, FICO_Crosswalk). TEETH: every crosswalk entry binds one or more `binds_ontology` terms; a term that is NOT a member of `governed_ontology` is REJECTED by gbrg.governance.supply_chain_risk.validate_crosswalk_term (a crosswalk cannot smuggle an ungoverned control term into the estate vocabulary).

governed_ontology.description: The estate-governed supply-chain-risk vocabulary. This is the SINGLE allow-list a crosswalk term may bind to. Node/edge/event/service terms are transcribed verbatim from the workbook 'Ontology' sheet; control families from 'Weights' + 'Controls_Evidence'; risk objects are the estate-owned scoring artifacts this contract produces.

bian_crosswalk.interpretation: BIAN is the bank operating-model anchor. Maps software-supply-chain risk objects to BIAN service domains so the framework can be discussed in recognized banking architecture terms.

entries.software_ormf_object: Risk taxonomy, scoring model, scenario design
entries.why: BIAN Operational Risk Models is the banking home for node/path/cluster scoring and scenario analysis.
BIAN Production Release evaluates production/business/operational risk before change is accepted.

entries.software_ormf_object: Standards for tooling, testing, and deployment
entries.why: BIAN IT Standards and Guidelines covers tooling, testing, deployment, platforms and IT policies.

entries.software_ormf_object: Security validation of controls and environments
entries.why: Security Assurance maintains assurance checks confirming countermeasures are in place and effective.

entries.software_ormf_object: Continuity, recovery, fallback, and exit planning
entries.why: Continuity Planning is the banking home for recovery objectives, rollback, mirror and provider-exit planning.
BIAN Procurement anchors registry, CI, cloud, model-provider and tool-vendor due diligence.

entries.software_ormf_object: Approved third-party universe and concentration view
entries.why: Approved Supplier Directory fits mirrored registries, approved package channels, CI providers, model/tool vendors.
Internal Audit is the banking owner for challenging assumptions, evidence freshness, exceptions and residual-risk statements.

fico_crosswalk.interpretation: FICO is the decisioning / customer-lifecycle anchor. Maps software-supply-chain risk objects to FICO platform capabilities, governance concepts, and lifecycle use cases.

entries.software_ormf_object: Inventory of critical nodes, decision assets, and dependencies
entries.why: FICO Platform manages decision assets and tracks dependencies/lineage — the analog to the node/path graph and evidence model.

entries.software_ormf_object: External providers, plugins, APIs, and ecosystem boundaries
entries.why: Anchors external model providers, tool servers, data providers, and integration trust boundaries.

entries.software_ormf_object: Governance of model-dependent and AI-dependent paths
entries.fico_capability: Responsible AI & Governance / FICO Responsible AI
entries.why: FICO Responsible AI covers building, executing, monitoring and governing models — AI/model-provider risk, evidence, auditability.

entries.software_ormf_object: Monitoring, KRIs, model/service drift, and operating feedback
entries.why: Continuous Feedback = real-time insight into business/system/model performance: the anchor for KRIs, KCIs, drift, degradation.

entries.software_ormf_object: Scenario analysis and ex-ante change impact testing
entries.fico_capability: Digital Twins & Simulation / Business Outcome Simulator
entries.why: Frames severe-but-plausible supply-chain scenarios and release simulations before making a change.
